profile.reading:
Per Vantage Data Centers' own press release, this building, VA13, sits on the Ashburn I campus at 45200 Vantage Data Plaza, Sterling, VA 20166. Vantage states VA13 spans 365,000 square feet and 44 megawatts of critical IT load; the operator was awarded a $300 million USD green loan for the facility, announced in July 2022, when the building was described as under development and scheduled to become operational that fall. At the time, Vantage described the campus as a 146-megawatt, 42-acre "mega campus" with five facilities planned, more than 1 million square feet across those five buildings once fully developed; Vantage's current campus page describes Ashburn I as having grown further to six data centers, 1.7 million square feet at full buildout, and 206 megawatts total.

Vantage is a private, Denver, Colorado-headquartered operator; DigitalBridge acquired the company in March 2017, and in January 2024 Vantage announced a $6.4 billion equity investment round led by DigitalBridge and Silver Lake. Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to every Ashburn-area facility: in November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates raising a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 data center rate class effective January 1, 2027, per Inside Climate News.

Northern Virginia's Loudoun and Prince William counties together form the largest data center market in the world by capacity, and local zoning debate has intensified as residents, county supervisors, and Dominion Energy weigh the tradeoff between substantial commercial tax revenue from facilities like this one and rising transmission-line construction, land consumption, and residential electricity-rate pressure tied to data center growth. Dominion Energy's long-range integrated resource plans have repeatedly cited this region's data center demand as the single largest driver of the utility's near-term generation and transmission capital spending, a dynamic that has also drawn scrutiny from the Virginia State Corporation Commission in periodic rate cases. Vantage's Virginia cluster sits among the densest concentration of competing operators anywhere in the world, including Amazon Web Services, Equinix, Digital Realty, and QTS facilities within a few miles.

reading.body:
Vantage VA13 is one building in the Ashburn I campus, a six-building, 52-acre facility in Sterling, Virginia. The operator publishes 206 MW of critical IT load and 1.7 million square feet across all six buildings at full buildout, with over 1 million square feet already operational. No figure specific to VA13 alone has been published, so this building's contribution to the campus total cannot be separated from available data.

At the campus-wide density of up to 300 W per square foot, the operator's stated 1.7 million square feet implies a potential IT load approaching the published 206 MW. Assuming 40 kW per rack as a common AI training density, 206 MW of IT load would correspond to roughly 5,150 racks; at higher densities typical of GPU clusters, that footprint would hold fewer, denser racks. The operator publishes no tenant list or power-per-building breakdown.

Virginia has 326 mapped data centers, 23 with published capacity figures totaling 1,375 MW. The Ashburn I campus, at 206 MW published, ranks 24th in the state by announced capacity, below the top 23 facilities with individual figures on the record. This facility sits in the Ashburn market, Northern Virginia's primary data center cluster, but remains below the threshold of published capacity that would place it among the state's ranked operators.
